title: PARPi-GaMD v3.8 — auditing enhanced-sampling rank associations: code, data and figures
description:
Replication package for a dual-system Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) study of PARP1 inhibitors and a six-part audit of descriptor–phenotype rank associations. System S1 (catalytic domain only) quantifies the HD–ART sampled-range span; system S2 (near-full-length PARP1–DNA) quantifies protein–DNA and HD–ART collective variables, spanning ten inhibitors and a ligand-free control, extended by three audited protonation-state re-simulations (13 S1 and 13 S2 systems).

The audit covers windowed estimator variance, estimator-consistency matrices, convergence–timescale scaling, ordinal sensitivity, counterfactual sensitivity, and ligand chemical state, paired with a planted-association benchmark and a design-stage power table for the exact tie-aware permutation test. The headline result is negative and reported as such: under the revision-primary C2/5–95% quantile estimator the neutral panel gives rho = +0.21 (exact p = 0.767, n = 5) and the protonation-state-corrected panel gives rho = +0.41 (p = 0.500); the prior C3/min–max convention gives rho = -0.15 (p = 0.833) and +0.21 (p = 0.767). No first-window cell reaches nominal significance. At n = 5 with one tied rank pair, p < 0.05 requires |rho| >= 0.975 and power at rho = 0.8 is about 14%, so the design excludes only |rho| approximately 0.9 or larger.

The release contains the full analysis and figure code chains, the archived data layer (per-frame boost-energy series, reweighting weights, PMF curves, curated panel tables), a per-artifact manifest mapping manuscript numbers to generating scripts, and a dependency-free tie-aware rank-association toolkit (tools/audit_assoc/) with CLI, documented CSV schema, worked example, and unit tests. The manuscript number audit returns 162/162 checks from a clean checkout.

Limitations: the rank-association analyses use a five-inhibitor panel (exact permutation, n = 5); production trajectories are 2-ns-window limited by design; raw production trajectories (~1 TB) are not distributed, and the release contains the derived data layer plus the tooling that regenerates every manuscript value.
